findings.evidence: Table 7-2 bottom note: "Any inference residency after* fine-tuning is a separate weights+KV question, priced by Table 7-1.)*"
findings.issue: Garbled/malformed text: a closing ')' and '*' are appended after the period with no matching opening '('. The intended footnote anchor was almost certainly just the word "after" — i.e. "after*" — but the stray ')*' makes the parenthetical unmatched.
findings.fix_instruction: Delete the trailing ')*' after 'Table 7-1.' so the note reads "Any inference residency after* fine-tuning is a separate weights+KV question, priced by Table 7-1."

findings.evidence: Preface (p. xix): "the ~64 GB runtime/workspace reserve (canonical scenario)[ASSUMPTION]"; Ch. 2 (p. 30): "the ~436 GB KV budget after the 140 GB of weights and the ~64 GB reserve (640 − 140 − 64 = 436). ... The reserve is introduced in Ch 4 and derived in Ch 7."
findings.issue: Preface-vs-body contradiction: the Preface labels the ~64 GB reserve as an [ASSUMPTION]; Ch. 7 §7.1 also labels it [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] and states plainly that 'The exact value must come from a deployment benchmark on the target stack'. Ch. 2 says it is 'derived in Ch 7', which is false — Ch. 7 assumes it and derives only the 436 GB budget that depends on it.
findings.fix_instruction: Change Ch. 2's 'derived in Ch 7' to 'assumed in Ch. 4 and Ch. 7, with the 436 GB KV budget derived from it in Ch. 7' so the two chapters agree on the reserve's epistemic status.

findings.evidence: Ch. 7 Table 7-2 note: "Fine-tuning residency adds optimizer states (Adam m, v, and master weights), which for 70B at ~16 bytes/param totals ~1,120 GB — roughly 1.75× the 640 GB of 8×H100." ... "The actual training peak is higher and is not inferable from that floor alone: it also includes activation memory..."
findings.issue: Arithmetic/consistency defect: 1,120 ÷ 640 = 1.75 is correct, but the same paragraph elsewhere in the chapter (§7.6) states the inference-vs-training gap as '≈6.8× (~164 GB at 9.2K vs ~1,120 GB)' — 1,120 ÷ 164 = 6.83, so the two multiples are arithmetically consistent but the chapter presents them as two 'multiples' with different denominators only in §7.6's footnote; §7.6's phrasing 'measured against the inference residency floor the same gap is ≈6.8×' coexists with 'roughly 1.75×' in §7.3 without a cross-reference, inviting a reader to read 1.75× and 6.8× as contradictory rather than as denominator-dependent statements.
findings.fix_instruction: In Table 7-2's note, state the denominator for each multiple inline (1.75× against host capacity; 6.8× against the ~164 GB inference floor) and add a one-clause pointer to §7.6 so the two figures cannot be read as a contradiction.

findings.evidence: Ch. 7 §7.4 item 1: "a model with 64 layers and 8192 dim will have ~2.1 MB/token at FP16 (2 × 64 × 8192 × 2 B = 2,097,152 B), while a model with 100 layers and 12288 dim will have ~4.9 MB/token (2 × 100 × 12288 × 2 B = 4,915,200 B)."
findings.issue: Rounding inconsistency: 2,097,152 B = 2.097152 decimal MB, printed '~2.1 MB' — fine; 4,915,200 B = 4.9152 decimal MB, printed '~4.9 MB' — fine. However Ch. 3 §3.6.1 (p. 46) states the same geometry as '~4.9 MB/token', and Ch. 3 §3.6.1 also claims 'It is not the largest KV constant in the book: Ch. 7 §7.4 re-derives the per-token value for other geometries, where a 100-layer, 12,288-hidden model at FP16 gives ~4.9 MB/token.' The two agree, so this is a non-defect worth recording only to confirm it was checked — no action beyond keeping the 4.9152 → 4.9 convention uniform.
findings.fix_instruction: No change required; ensure the same decimal-MB rounding convention (truncate-to-one-decimal) is applied to the 4,915,200 B figure wherever it recurs.

findings.evidence: "2×H100 total VRAM | 2 ×80 GB = 160 GB | [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)"; "8×H100 total VRAM | 8 ×80 GB = 640 GB | [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)"; "3×H100 total VRAM | 3 ×80 GB = 240 GB | 3 × 80 GB; vendor constant [1P][DERIVED] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)".
findings.issue: Identical arithmetic (N × 80 GB) is tagged [1P][FACT] on two rows and [1P][DERIVED] on the third. The vendor FACT is the 80 GB per-part constant; the products are derived in every row — three parallel rows, inconsistent tags.
findings.fix_instruction: Tag all three products [1P][DERIVED] from the [1P][FACT] 80 GB constant (or all [1P][FACT], if the intended policy is that host aggregates inherit the datasheet tag) — pick one and apply to all rows.

findings.evidence: "the per-rank test still fails (70 + 12.05 (per-rank FP16 KV, 24.1 ÷ 2) + ~8 GB reserve = 90.05 GB > 85.5 GB), so the ≥3-GPU conclusion is unchanged" (PDF 152–153). The 128K row defines the per-rank reserve as "the full runtime-reserve share 64 ÷ 8 = 8 GB … the 8 GB is the whole ~64 GB host reserve divided across the ranks" (PDF 158).
findings.issue: The vendor-binary per-rank test borrows the 8-rank per-rank share (~8 GB) for a 2-rank host, where the book's own division rule gives 64 ÷ 2 = 32 GB. The fail verdict survives (70 + 12.05 + 32 = 114.05 > 85.5), but the stated reserve term is inconsistent with the book's definition of the per-rank share.
findings.fix_instruction: Use the 2-rank share (64 ÷ 2 = 32 GB) in the vendor-binary per-rank test and update the printed sum.

findings.evidence: "the qualifier that the gain is highly prompt-size-dependent is this book's own inference from the benchmark's description, not a source-reported figure [1P][DERIVED]".
findings.issue: The claim is a qualitative inference, not 'computed by arithmetic from stated inputs' (the book's definition of DERIVED); by the book's own taxonomy a reasoned-but-unvalidated reading is [HYPOTHESIS].
findings.fix_instruction: Retag as [1P][HYPOTHESIS], or drop the tag and carry the uncertainty in prose.
